source.title: Enhancing Transformers without Self-supervised Learning: A Loss Landscape Perspective in Sequential Recommendation
source.authors: V. Lai; Huiyuan Chen; Chin-Chia Michael Yeh; Minghua Xu; Yi-Wei Cai; Hao Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The flattened Table 1 does not preserve every model-to-value assignment clearly enough to extract all baseline results.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sharpness-aware training to sequential recommenders, a new setting for loss-geometry and generalization claims, and reports held-out recommendation results.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for SAMRec and SAMRec variants on held-out recommendation metrics, and describes loss-landscape comparisons. It does not test the listed versions' classification claims or measure a train-test error gap. Its cited generalization results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization connection to motivate SAMRec and evaluates its recommendation performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against train–test gaps, compare generalization measures, or test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that self-supervised recommenders have smoother loss surfaces than SASRec and that SAMRec improves benchmark recommendation performance without requiring pre-training or strong data augmentation. Their attribution of these gains to smoother geometry is their interpretation; the study does not establish V7's sharpness–gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Sequential recommendation task; SAM min-max training with SASRec backbone; next-item recommendation metrics rather than classification error or train-test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAMRec radius ρ affects HR@10; authors report stable results across datasets when ρ is around [0.1, 1.0]. Results also differ by dataset and metric, including the Beauty exception.

fits_no_version.finding: SAMRec exceeds SASRec on both recommendation metrics across all four datasets. It exceeds CL4SRec on all listed comparisons except Beauty NDCG@10. Adding SAMRec to S3Rec or CL4SRec improves HR@10 across all four datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware min-max training can improve held-out sequential recommendation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.5 and Figure 1 describe smoother random-direction loss landscapes for self-supervised recommenders and SAMRec than for SASRec, without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness or train–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-supervised and sharpness-aware training can produce smoother visualized loss landscapes in Transformer sequential recommenders.

record.problems: No training error or train-test gap is reported. Landscape evidence is visualized along two random directions; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The text's flattened Table 1 impedes reliable assignment of the Sports NDCG@10 values.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 reports reduced-training-data comparisons only as plots; the text says SAMRec consistently outperforms SASRec and CL4SRec across datasets, but exact values are not stated, so those results are not extracted as rows. Figure 3 gives radius-sweep values only in plots. Figure 1 landscape comparisons do not report a train-test gap or a numeric sharpness measure and are not rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured train–test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm and margin measures. Random-direction landscape plots and recommendation metrics do not establish these relationships.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, rather than judgments that the recommendation improvements are unreadable. These method-performance comparisons belong under fits_no_version. Results average ten independent runs, but no uncertainty estimates are supplied. Table 2's prose understates its improvement range: the listed Toys S3Rec gain is 6.03%.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on MNIST or CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization on image or language benchmarks.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.

Magnitude-aware sharpness and measured train-test gaps within a convolutional family; the paper uses random-direction loss-landscape visualizations and does not measure the specified gap or compare the specified measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
